name: Gold time-of-day: long 11:00 to 02:00, short 02:00 to 11:00 New York

why: +0.646 R/trade over 20 trades, PF 1.769, passes every screen

source: Donati & Jung, 'Gold Price Dynamics Around the Clock', MSc thesis, Copenhagen Business School 2019; COMEX gold
original_rules: Long: buy at 11:00, sell at 02:00 the next day (New York time). Short: short at 02:00, cover at 11:00. Combo: both. No stops.
implementation: The combo, as stated; both legs are also reported separately.
deviations: Spot XAUUSD instead of COMEX futures.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

execution.costs: frozen Phase 5 cost model: candle spread (0.30 fallback), commission 3.50 USD/lot/side, slippage 0.05 USD per fill
execution.r_unit: The source has no stop: R is a NOMINAL unit of 1.5 x ATR(14) on M15 at entry (GoldScalp's default ATR stop size). Marked nominal; USD results are always reported too.

range.note: The same 14 calendar days (10 trading days) as stage 1. Classification uses this window only.

Supplementary, about 11 weeks of the same spent development series. Once-a-day rules cannot reach 15 trades in 10 trading days; this run shows more trades for them. It does not classify anything and is not validation.

evidence_at_registration.note: Both windows are development data. The context window contains the screen days.

assessment: It met the declared screen rule on 10 trading days, which is why it is registered. The 11-week context run does not support it: about zero in R and a loss in USD, with the long leg losing. Not recommended for further work unless a new reason appears.
caveats: Outside the 10 screen days it made -0.132 R per trade over 90 trades.
Month by month it swung from -22 R to +22 R: no steady effect.
Positions are held 9 and 15 hours without a stop; R is a nominal unit.
The source's own net-of-cost effect is small and decaying.
next_questions: Is there any regime in which the long leg works, as the source claims?
restrictions: Screening only: not validated, not shown to be profitable, not trading-ready.
Its Strategy Lab form (LAB_STRATEGIES.json) was added on 16 November 2026 at the owner's request. Live or demo results of that form are not a validation of this candidate.
The rules are frozen as screened. A changed rule is a new candidate with a new id.
Development data already used for it: 20 July to 31 October 2026. Those months are not validation data.
Any validation must use data research has not touched (forward data from 14 November 2026) under a registered, frozen protocol.

archived.reason: At the owner's request, P7-FIX stays the only active research candidate. P7-TOD passed the 10-day screen (+0.646 nominal R per trade over 20 trades) but did not hold over the 11-week run (+0.009 R, -$326 over 110 trades): the long leg lost $588, the short leg made $262. Its record, rules and evidence are kept unchanged; it is not deleted.
archived.strategy_lab: Both legs archived in Strategy Lab (strategies 5 and 6); their versions are kept.
